migrations.reason: older catalog set SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB to 0xFFFFFFFF (every service in shared svchost, the "forced" mode ReviOS itself avoids because it breaks XboxGipSvc); ReviOS ships the Windows default 0x380000, so the entry was removed

tweaks.description: Create a restore point (bypass the 24h frequency limit) before any run; engine also writes a JSON state snapshot.
tweaks.explanation: Creates a Windows restore point before the first change (lifting the 24-hour limit for this one call) so you can roll back with System Restore. The engine does this itself.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users with a specific need
tweaks.tradeoff: Needs System Protection turned on for C:. Takes a few seconds and some disk space; if it fails the run is aborted.

tweaks.description: Enable daily periodic registry backup (RegIdleBackup).
tweaks.explanation: Turns the periodic registry backup (RegIdleBackup task) back on so a copy of the registry hives is saved on a schedule.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who want to control background tasks
tweaks.tradeoff: Uses a little disk space and a short background task. Nothing is lost.

tweaks.description: Set diagnostic data policy to minimum. Honoured as 0 only on Enterprise/Education; Pro/Home treat it as Required (1).
tweaks.breaks: Insider builds need telemetry
tweaks.measuredEffect: Microsoft-disclosed (secondhand, Win10 1703): Basic about 109-159 KB/day, Enhanced about 239-348 KB/day. Not a packet capture.
tweaks.explanation: Sets the diagnostic data level to the minimum. On Windows 11 Pro and Home, 0 is treated as Required (1), so you cannot reach a true off state. Real traffic at Required is already tiny.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users on any edition; real 'off' only on Enterprise, Education or Server
tweaks.tradeoff: On Windows 11 Pro/Home, 0 is treated as Required (1), so the real effect differs from the label; only Enterprise/Education honour 0. Microsoft warns that fully off omits Windows Update failure information. tiny11 and ReviOS both write 0 as well; on Pro and Business the effective level is Required (1), so the label "off" overstates it. The engine now says so in the plan row on those editions instead of reporting a plain Verified.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Can conflict with the Intune diagnostics-data policy and with Windows Update for Business / Autopatch reporting, which need at least Required data.

appliesTo.reason: AllowTelemetry=0 is only honoured on Enterprise, Education and Server; Pro and Business treat it as 1 (Required data), so the value written is not the level that takes effect

tweaks.description: Atlas also sets AllowTelemetry/MaxTelemetryAllowed under CurrentVersion\Policies and Wow6432Node plus AllowDeviceNameInTelemetry.
tweaks.explanation: Writes the same diagnostic level to extra registry locations. It mostly duplicates the main policy and adds little on its own.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who want the policy applied redundantly
tweaks.tradeoff: Little extra effect; more keys to keep track of.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Can conflict with the Intune diagnostics-data policy and WUfB / Autopatch reporting.

appliesTo.reason: AllowTelemetry/MaxTelemetryAllowed 0 are only honoured on Enterprise, Education and Server; elsewhere the effective level is Required (1)

tweaks.description: Stop OneSettings configuration downloads.
tweaks.explanation: Stops OneSettings configuration downloads. Microsoft says settings-win.data.microsoft.com sends no diagnostic data and is used for remote configuration, so blocking it saves almost nothing.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy purists
tweaks.tradeoff: Microsoft advises against blocking this endpoint. It may delay remote fixes and feature config.

tweaks.description: Hide feedback notifications.
tweaks.explanation: Hides feedback pop-ups. A nuisance fix, not a traffic or CPU saver.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone annoyed by prompts
tweaks.tradeoff: None meaningful.

tweaks.description: Disable event transcript / mini trace slot and delete DiagTrack ETL logs.
tweaks.explanation: Turns off the local diagnostic event transcript and mini trace slot, and marks the diagnostic-data toast as already shown.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users
tweaks.tradeoff: The Diagnostic Data Viewer keeps less history, and there is less local diagnostic data for Microsoft support to look at.

tweaks.description: Disable WMI autologgers Diagtrack-Listener, SQMLogger, SetupPlatformTel.
tweaks.explanation: Stops three background trace sessions (Diagtrack-Listener, SQMLogger, SetupPlatformTel) from starting at boot.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users
tweaks.tradeoff: Less local diagnostic tracing for troubleshooting; takes effect after a restart. Admin tools that read those traces have nothing to read.
tweaks.managedSkip: DiagTrack and its autologgers feed Intune Endpoint analytics, Windows Update reports and Autopatch.

tweaks.description: Disable Customer Experience Improvement Program.
tweaks.explanation: Turns off the Customer Experience Improvement Program, which sends anonymous usage data to Microsoft.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users
tweaks.tradeoff: Microsoft gets less usage data from this PC. No visible loss. A policy from your organisation may already set it.

tweaks.description: Disable Windows Error Reporting.
tweaks.breaks: No crash reports; harder to troubleshoot with Microsoft tooling
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured; Windows Error Reporting only sends data after a crash, so idle impact is nil
tweaks.explanation: Turns off Windows Error Reporting so crash data is not collected or sent. It is a privacy choice, not a speed gain.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users
tweaks.tradeoff: Lose crash dumps and Microsoft fix suggestions.

tweaks.description: Outbound firewall block for DiagTrack and WerSvc services.

implementation.run: New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'Tool Block DiagTrack' -Direction Outbound -Action Block -Service DiagTrack; New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'Tool Block WerSvc' -Direction Outbound -Action Block -Service WerSvc

tweaks.breaks: Windows Update diagnostics, error reporting and Windows Update for Business reporting.
tweaks.explanation: Adds outbound firewall blocks for the telemetry and error reporting services. The data volume is small and Microsoft notes some traffic still appears in captures.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who want a belt-and-braces block
tweaks.tradeoff: Blocks the DiagTrack and WerSvc services from the network. Can break Windows Update diagnostics, error reporting and Windows Update for Business reporting.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Can interfere with Intune/Defender diagnostics and Windows Update reporting. Note: this entry is a firewall command, which the engine skips.
tweaks.managedSkip: DiagTrack and its autologgers feed Intune Endpoint analytics, Windows Update reports and Autopatch.

tweaks.description: Opt out of .NET CLI and PowerShell telemetry (machine env vars).
tweaks.explanation: Sets two machine-wide environment variables so the .NET command-line tools and PowerShell do not send usage telemetry.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users
tweaks.tradeoff: No loss for everyday use. Only affects developer tools, and only for programs started after the change.

tweaks.description: Turn off ads, suggestions and silent app installs for the user (also apply to Default user hive).

revert.note: restoreSnapshot per value; stock is 1 or absent

tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured; fewer ads and suggestions rather than speed. Areas rated 1 and 2.
tweaks.explanation: Stops Windows from showing suggested apps, tips and promotions in Start, Settings and the lock screen, and from silently installing promoted apps. Mainly a cleaner desktop with a bit less background network traffic.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone annoyed by ads and suggestions in Windows, especially new installs
tweaks.tradeoff: You stop seeing tips and suggested apps. Some of the policies are not supported on Pro per the Policy CSP table, and the policy does not cover every per-user Spotlight toggle. ReviOS also writes these under HKU\.DEFAULT; that is the LocalSystem profile (logon screen), not the template for new users, so it is not done here. New-user defaults need the offline C:\Users\Default\NTUSER.DAT.

tweaks.description: Block consumer experiences / suggested app installs by policy.
tweaks.explanation: Blocks consumer experiences, meaning auto-installed promotional apps that appear after setup or updates. Keeps Start tidy and avoids downloads you did not ask for.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Fresh installs, shared PCs and Enterprise/Education editions
tweaks.tradeoff: Microsoft honours this policy on Enterprise/Education; Pro behaviour is uncertain. Must be set within 15 minutes of install or baked into an image to take effect. Little performance gain.

tweaks.description: Disable advertising ID, tailored experiences, ink/typing harvesting.
tweaks.explanation: Turns off the advertising ID, tailored experiences based on diagnostic data, and implicit ink and typing collection.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users

tweaks.description: Disable activity feed, publishing and upload of user activities.
tweaks.explanation: Turns off the activity feed and stops this PC from publishing or uploading your activity history.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users
tweaks.tradeoff: Features that resume activity across your devices stop working. History already collected is not deleted.
tweaks.notes: Winutil lists EnableActivityFeed=1 which conflicts with the intent; 0 is used here.

tweaks.description: Disable Cross-Device Platform.
tweaks.breaks: Nearby sharing / cross-device resume

tweaks.whoBenefits: Users with no Bluetooth/Nearby Sharing/Phone Link use
tweaks.tradeoff: Nearby Sharing, Phone Link and some device pairing features stop working.

tweaks.description: Stop tracking app launches for Start suggestions.
tweaks.breaks: Start 'most used' list empty
tweaks.explanation: Stops Windows from recording which apps you launch to rank Start suggestions. A privacy setting with no measurable speed change.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users
tweaks.tradeoff: Start shows fewer personalized recommendations.

tweaks.description: Remove Bing web results/Cortana/location use from Windows Search by policy.
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured; reports say Start search waits on Microsoft servers before showing local results, with the biggest gain on older PCs
tweaks.explanation: Stops the Start menu from sending your typing to Bing and waiting for web results. Local apps and files then show up faster and web clutter goes away. One of the few shell tweaks you can actually feel.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who uses Start search for apps and files, especially on older PCs and slow connections
tweaks.tradeoff: You lose web answers in Start such as weather, unit conversion and web suggestions. On some builds DisableSearchBoxSuggestions does not fully suppress web results.

tweaks.description: Stop online font provider downloads.
tweaks.explanation: Stops Windows from downloading fonts on demand from Microsoft online font providers.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users
tweaks.tradeoff: Documents that rely on a cloud font show a substitute font until you install it yourself.

tweaks.description: Stop disk health model downloads.
tweaks.explanation: Stops Windows from downloading updated disk-health prediction models.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users
tweaks.tradeoff: Disk-health warnings use the model already on the PC, which may become slightly out of date.

tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured. Microsoft describes the cloud payload as small and sent only when local engines cannot decide.
tweaks.explanation: Turns off Defender cloud reporting and sample submission. Traffic is small, so you save almost nothing, while protection against new threats gets weaker.

tweaks.breaks: Warnings about Defender, firewall, UAC and Windows Update problems no longer pop up, so a protection that has switched off is easy to miss.
tweaks.explanation: Hides Security and Maintenance pop-up notifications. This reduces noise but also hides warnings.
tweaks.whoBenefits: People who find those pop-ups annoying
tweaks.tradeoff: You may miss useful security alerts.

tweaks.description: Disable the Office Telemetry Agent scheduled tasks (explicit names only).
tweaks.explanation: Turns off the scheduled tasks that run the Office Telemetry Agent (the optional Telemetry Dashboard collector). Only these four task names are touched. The Office Automatic Updates, ClickToRun Service Monitor and subscription tasks in the same folder are NOT touched. Microsoft Learn documents OfficeTelemetryAgentLogOn; the FallBack and 2016 variants are the same agent on other Office builds and are skipped if absent.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Home or small-office users who do not use the Office Telemetry Dashboard
tweaks.tradeoff: If your organisation uses the Office Telemetry Dashboard, this PC stops reporting to it. Office itself and its updates are unaffected.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Only relevant where an admin runs the Telemetry Dashboard; otherwise none.
tweaks.managedSkip: Microsoft 365 Apps are managed by IT.

tweaks.description: Disable telemetry scheduled tasks (ProgramDataUpdater, CEIP, Chkdsk Proxy, WER QueueReporting). The Compatibility Appraiser is a separate tweak.
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured. The CPU and disk bursts people report come from the Compatibility Appraiser, which is now the separate tweak task-compat-appraiser-off.
tweaks.explanation: Disables four small telemetry scheduled tasks: ProgramDataUpdater, the Customer Experience Improvement Program tasks, the Chkdsk proxy and Windows Error Reporting QueueReporting. None of them take part in update compatibility gating. The Compatibility Appraiser, the best-known source of CompatTelRunner bursts, is kept out of the safe preset in task-compat-appraiser-off because feature-update gating depends on it. tiny11 deletes the same task files; disabling them is the reversible equivalent (the task XML and its TaskCache entries stay intact).
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who want less background telemetry activity
tweaks.tradeoff: Evidence is forum and vendor articles, not Microsoft data. Windows may re-enable the tasks. tiny11 deletes these task files, which cannot be undone; disabling is the reversible equivalent.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: These tasks do not feed update gating. Customer Experience Improvement Program and error reporting data may still be collected centrally by your organisation.

tweaks.description: Disable the Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser scheduled task.
tweaks.breaks: Feature-update compatibility safeguard holds and Update Compliance / Autopatch readiness data, which are built from the Appraiser results.
tweaks.measuredEffect: Anecdotal CPU and disk spikes up to about 20 minutes from CompatTelRunner; no benchmark. Areas rated 1 and 3; reconciled to 2.
tweaks.explanation: Disables the Compatibility Appraiser, the best-known source of CompatTelRunner CPU and disk bursts on weaker PCs. It is not in the safe preset because Windows uses its results to decide whether a PC can receive a feature update: without it the safeguard holds that protect a PC with a known-bad driver or app cannot work, and readiness reports go blank.
tweaks.whoBenefits: HDD, low-end or older PCs with startup or idle spikes that you update by hand
tweaks.tradeoff: Windows upgrade readiness checks and feature-update gating can behave differently because the Compatibility Appraiser is disabled; Windows may re-enable the task. Evidence is forum and vendor articles, not Microsoft data. tiny11 deletes this task file, which cannot be undone; disabling is the reversible equivalent.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: The Appraiser feeds feature-update readiness and compatibility gating that Windows Update for Business / Autopatch rely on.
tweaks.managedSkip: The Compatibility Appraiser feeds feature-update safeguard holds and Update Compliance / Autopatch readiness that IT relies on.

tweaks.description: Stop and disable Connected User Experiences and Telemetry.
tweaks.measuredEffect: PCGH (May 2025, 7800X3D, standard vs Nano 11 debloat): average gaming FPS unchanged. Microsoft-disclosed telemetry volume at Required level about 100-160 KB/day (old, Win10 1703). Background reviewers report steadier memory but no numbers. Areas rated this 0-2; reconciled to 1.
tweaks.explanation: Stops the telemetry service (Connected User Experiences and Telemetry). Windows Update, activation and Defender keep working. It is mainly a privacy measure: traffic is small and a controlled test showed no FPS change.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users; people who see CompatTelRunner or telemetry spikes
tweaks.tradeoff: Pauses compatibility telemetry and Feedback Hub. May interfere with Insider enrollment. Windows can re-enable it after updates. Deleting the service (some scripts do) can block ESU enrollment; disabling is safer.
tweaks.managedSkip: DiagTrack and its autologgers feed Intune Endpoint analytics, Windows Update reports and Autopatch.

tweaks.description: Disable WerSvc, PcaSvc, diagnosticshub collector, wercplsupport.
tweaks.breaks: No Program Compatibility Assistant prompts, no crash reports
tweaks.ram_or_perf_effect: Fewer background services; hard to quantify
tweaks.explanation: Disables error reporting and the program compatibility assistant. These are small services that mostly sleep, so the saving is tiny.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-focused users
tweaks.tradeoff: No crash reports or compatibility prompts for old programs, which makes troubleshooting harder.

tweaks.description: ReviOS extra set: WdiServiceHost, WdiSystemHost, dam, wisvc, Wecsvc.
tweaks.breaks: Built-in troubleshooters, Insider enrollment; some are protected and need registry Start=4
tweaks.explanation: Disables diagnostic policy hosts, desktop activity moderator, Insider service and event collector. Mostly idle services.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Tweakers on gaming-only PCs
tweaks.tradeoff: Built-in troubleshooters stop working; Insider builds break; the activity moderator also manages power behavior.
tweaks.notes: DPS and diagsvc are not part of the ReviOS playbook defaults; Revision Tool offers them under its "Usage Reporting" toggle together with SleepStudy logging.

tweaks.explanation: Disables mail/contacts sync and link tracking. Small services.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users with no Mail/Calendar app sync
tweaks.tradeoff: Mail, People and Calendar apps stop syncing.

tweaks.explanation: Disable UCPD driver and its scheduled task (reboot needed).

tweaks.description: Disable NetBT, GpuEnergyDrv, tcpipreg and Telemetry driver entries (registry Start=4, reboot).

tweaks.explanation: Disable NetBT, GpuEnergyDrv, tcpipreg and Telemetry driver entries (registry Start=4, reboot).
tweaks.whoBenefits: Tweakers who want fewer background services
tweaks.tradeoff: NetBIOS name resolution, legacy SMB discovery; tcpipreg is flagged experimental by ReviOS. Undo is exact (snapshot). Stock NetBT is Start=1 (System).

tweaks.description: Set the Edge updater service (edgeupdate) to Manual instead of disabling it.
tweaks.explanation: Sets the Edge update service to start on demand instead of at boot. Edge still updates itself through its own scheduled update tasks; this does not disable updating.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Everyone, as a safe default
tweaks.tradeoff: Edge updates can be delayed if the updater tasks are also disabled; Manual alone normally does not stop updates.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Edge updates may be governed by Intune or Edge update policy; check with your admin.

tweaks.description: Set the console driver (condrv) to start automatically (fix for error 0xd000003a).
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured; a stability fix, not a speed-up
tweaks.explanation: Sets the Windows console driver service to start automatically. Reported as a fix for console apps failing with 0xd000003a after other services were changed. It is only useful if you hit that error.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Only people who see error 0xd000003a in console apps
tweaks.tradeoff: Changes a kernel-driver start type for a problem most PCs do not have.

tweaks.description: Set WSAIFabricSvc to Manual (or Disabled) to avoid AI fabric autostart.
tweaks.explanation: Stops the Windows AI Fabric service from starting automatically. Safe because Manual still allows on-demand start.
tweaks.whoBenefits: PCs not using Windows AI features or without an NPU
tweaks.tradeoff: None for most users. Disabled (rather than Manual) can break AI features. Only source is Win11Debloat release notes.

tweaks.description: Disable hibernation (and Fast Startup). Skip on laptops by default.
tweaks.breaks: No hibernate; sleep heat on some modern-standby laptops (playbook #116, #199)
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured; frees the hibernation file disk space
tweaks.explanation: Turns off hibernation, which also removes the hibernation file and disables Fast Startup. You get disk space back but lose hibernate and faster boots.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Small-SSD desktops that never hibernate and need the disk space
tweaks.tradeoff: Boots slower (same cost as disabling Fast Startup) and you lose hibernate. Bad for laptops. hiberfil.sys is 40 % of RAM by default (about 12.8 GB on a 32 GB PC). "powercfg /h /type reduced" keeps Fast Startup and uses about 20 % of RAM (about 6.4 GB), at the cost of full hibernate and hybrid sleep.
tweaks.notes: Reduced hiberfile type (powercfg /h /type reduced) is the safer disk saving: it keeps Fast Startup (see pwr-hiberfile-reduced). ReviOS turns hibernation off entirely and its own file warns about overheating in sleep on Modern Standby laptops. Implemented natively: the engine snapshots the exact hibernation state (off, reduced or full) and undo puts that state back.

appliesTo.reason: laptops keep hibernate (it saves the session when the battery runs out); use pwr-hiberfile-reduced there

tweaks.description: Reduce the hibernation file to the Fast Startup type (powercfg /h /type reduced).
tweaks.breaks: Hibernate and hybrid sleep stop working (the reduced file only holds the Fast Startup session); Fast Startup keeps working
tweaks.ram_or_perf_effect: Frees about half of hiberfil.sys (40 % of RAM becomes about 20 %)
tweaks.measuredEffect: Microsoft: hiberfil.sys defaults to 40 % of RAM and the reduced type to about 20 %, so on a 32 GB PC about 12.8 GB becomes about 6.4 GB (about 6.4 GB freed). The engine shows free disk space before and after the change.
tweaks.explanation: Keeps Fast Startup but stores only the kernel session in the hibernation file, which is about half the size. You get several GB of disk back without turning Fast Startup off.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Laptops and desktops with a small SSD that boot with Fast Startup but never hibernate
tweaks.tradeoff: Full hibernate (saving all open apps to disk) and hybrid sleep stop working. If hibernation is currently off the tweak is skipped, because turning it on would use disk space.
tweaks.notes: Native handler: snapshot of the hibernation state (off, reduced or full) so undo restores the exact previous type. The recommended laptop alternative to pwr-hibernate-off (which only applies on desktops).

tweaks.description: Compress the Windows installation in place (compact /CompactOS:always).
tweaks.breaks: Takes 10-30 minutes of disk and CPU; a little decompression CPU on slow machines. A state Windows chose itself (not beneficial) is restored as an explicit 'never'.
tweaks.measuredEffect: Microsoft documents about 3.7-4.75 GB saved on x64 (CompactOS table). Microsoft also says it is unnecessary on fast NVMe storage and does not enable it there by default. The engine shows free disk space before and after.
tweaks.explanation: Stores Windows system files compressed (XPRESS4K). You get several GB of disk back; files are decompressed on the fly when read.
tweaks.whoBenefits: PCs with a small or nearly full system drive
tweaks.tradeoff: The run takes 10-30 minutes and uses CPU and disk. On fast NVMe drives Microsoft considers it unnecessary. Not in the safe preset. Windows may decide on its own not to keep the Compact state (the query then says 'not beneficial').
tweaks.notes: Native handler: Get parses 'compact /CompactOS:query' (English text, never the exit code, which is 102 for 'not compact'). Skipped while a restart or servicing is pending.

tweaks.description: Disable Fast Startup (hybrid boot).
tweaks.ram_or_perf_effect: Clean cold boots; slightly slower boot on HDD
tweaks.measuredEffect: Single-machine test: about 4 s boot with Fast Startup on vs about 9-10 s off (NVMe). Unverified estimate: 10-30 s slower depending on drive. Areas rated 0 and 1.; MakeUseOf (single author, SSD): shutdown-to-desktop about 11 s to 13 s
tweaks.explanation: Makes Shut down a real full shutdown instead of a hybrid hibernate. This clears stale state and avoids odd issues with updates, drivers or dual boot. It is a stability / clean-boot tweak and makes boot SLOWER, not faster.
tweaks.whoBenefits: People with dual boot, shutdown or update glitches
tweaks.tradeoff: Slower boot from Shut down (about 4 s with Fast Startup on vs 9-10 s off in one NVMe test, more on slower disks). Restart is unaffected.

tweaks.description: Create custom high-performance plan from the Ultimate Performance base and activate it (desktops only).
tweaks.breaks: Higher idle power and heat; unsuitable for battery laptops
tweaks.measuredEffect: ComputerBase 2017 (Ryzen 1800X, Win10, confounded with HPET): about 2% geometric mean, up to about 17% in one game, 0% in four titles; idle power 53 W vs 62 W. Mostly a core-parking issue on first-gen Ryzen, since fixed. No controlled modern frame-time data found.
tweaks.explanation: Keeps the CPU at high clocks and stops it parking cores or dropping speed when idle, so there is less ramp-up delay when work arrives. On modern CPUs the average difference is usually within noise but it can reduce stutter in some CPU-bound scenes.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Desktop users with latency-sensitive workloads (games, audio) who can accept higher idle power and heat
tweaks.tradeoff: Higher idle power, heat and fan noise. Not for laptops on battery. Benchmark three runs per plan before keeping it.
tweaks.notes: Uses a DebloatKit-owned plan GUID (deb10a7c-17a1-4e2d-9c3f-5a6b7c8d9e01). It previously reused 3ff9831b-6f80-4830-8178-736cd4229e7b, the legacy ReviOS plan that current Revision Tool deletes. ReviOS now duplicates the Ultimate Performance scheme as 6a93ec26-284d-4943-9fc4-c9616def55c6 and also sets processor thresholds, core parking and USB 3 link power; DebloatKit does not set those. The PERFINC/PERFDEC thresholds are no-ops on CPUs with hardware P-states (HWP), and core parking was fixed in Windows since the 2017 Ryzen results. Native handler: the snapshot records the active scheme and whether the DebloatKit plan already existed; undo re-activates that scheme and deletes the plan only when this run created it. If the Ultimate Performance base scheme does not exist (Modern Standby systems), the step fails with the powercfg error and changes nothing.

appliesTo.reason: high-performance plans drain a laptop battery and raise heat; the description has always said desktops only

tweaks.description: Activate Balanced plan.
tweaks.measuredEffect: Not measured on modern hardware; Balanced vs High Performance showed about 2% on a 2017 Ryzen setup, mostly from the old core-parking issue.
tweaks.explanation: Restores the default Balanced plan, which saves power at idle. On current CPUs it gives almost the same gaming speed as high-performance plans.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Laptops and anyone who wants lower idle power and noise without losing real gaming speed
tweaks.tradeoff: Possibly a few percent lower in rare CPU-bound scenes on some systems.

tweaks.description: Disable memory compression (reboot).
tweaks.breaks: More paging on low-RAM systems
tweaks.ram_or_perf_effect: Slight CPU saving, slightly more RAM use
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured as a gain; Microsoft Q&A report of about 1 GB held by compression on 16 GB, and disabling it increases pagefile use
tweaks.explanation: Disables RAM compression. It trades a little CPU for memory pressure, with no benchmark showing a gaming gain. It can hurt on 8 GB machines.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Systems with 32 GB or more where it is harmless but unneeded
tweaks.tradeoff: More paging on low-RAM systems. Disabling compression worsens commit and paging pressure, because pages that were compressed in RAM go to the pagefile instead. ReviOS disables memory compression by default (Disable-MMAgent -mc) and never re-enables it. On a PC with high commit charge this increases pagefile writes; do not use it there.
tweaks.notes: Lowers the "in use" number in Task Manager by moving pages to the pagefile instead of compressing them in RAM; it is accounting, not a gain. Never recommended for a commit-pressured PC. Native handler: Get-MMAgent / Disable-MMAgent -MemoryCompression, undo is Enable-MMAgent. When the commit charge is 80 % or more the plan row carries a warning (the step is not skipped); it takes effect after a restart.

tweaks.description: Disable NTFS last-access updates.
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured; catalog note: Fewer metadata writes
tweaks.explanation: Stops NTFS from updating the last-accessed time stamp each time a file is read, which saves a few small disk writes.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who want to fine-tune Windows behaviour
tweaks.tradeoff: Last-access times are no longer reliable; some backup, search and forensic tools that use them behave differently. Takes effect after a restart.

tweaks.description: Disable 8.3 short-name creation.
tweaks.breaks: Legacy installers / backup tools relying on 8.3 names
tweaks.explanation: Disable 8.3 short-name creation.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who want to fine-tune Windows behaviour
tweaks.tradeoff: Legacy installers / backup tools relying on 8.3 names
tweaks.notes: Native handler on the system-wide setting (fsutil behavior disable8dot3: 0 = on for all volumes, 1 = off for all, 2 = per volume, 3 = off except the system volume). The snapshot keeps the exact previous value, so undo restores it (not a fixed 2). Short names that already exist are not stripped. See perf-ntfs-8dot3-volume-off for the per-volume flag.

tweaks.description: Disable 8.3 short-name creation on each fixed NTFS volume (fsutil 8dot3name set <volume> 1).
tweaks.breaks: Legacy installers / backup tools relying on 8.3 names
tweaks.explanation: Turns off 8.3 short-name creation per volume. Only takes effect while the system-wide setting is 2 (per volume); otherwise the plan skips it and says so.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who want the per-volume form instead of the system-wide setting
tweaks.tradeoff: Legacy installers / backup tools relying on 8.3 names. Short names that already exist are not stripped.
tweaks.notes: One plan row per volume (the step target '*' expands to every fixed NTFS volume). Native handler with a per-volume snapshot.

tweaks.description: Foreground priority boost (38 / 0x26).
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured; no controlled FPS, frametime or input-lag benchmark of 0x26 (38) vs the default found on Win10 or Win11
tweaks.explanation: Windows already gives the window you are using a short priority boost. This setting changes how long programs run before the scheduler switches. 0x26 is what the Control Panel 'best performance for programs' option writes, so it is safe, but nobody has shown a measurable gain.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who run one heavy foreground app on a saturated CPU; most people will not notice
tweaks.tradeoff: Background tasks such as indexing or encoding get a little less CPU while you work. Community advice on 'best' values is trial and error, not data.

tweaks.description: Shorten shutdown/hang timeouts, zero menu delay.
tweaks.breaks: Apps killed before saving on shutdown (AutoEndTasks)
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured; only a perceived speedup is reported for MenuShowDelay=0 (default commonly cited as 400 ms)
tweaks.explanation: Shortens how long Windows waits for stuck apps and services at shutdown, and removes the hover delay before cascading menus open. The menu part is cosmetic and only affects classic Win32 menus.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users whose shutdowns hang on unresponsive apps, or who dislike the cascading menu delay
tweaks.tradeoff: Shorter shutdown timeouts can cut off apps that are still saving data. Submenus may open accidentally while moving the mouse. The 1500 ms (service) and 2000 ms (app and hang) figures come from the ReviOS documentation on revi.cc. They are not present in any file of the ReviOS playbook source that was checked, so treat them as unverified. revi.cc gives 1500 ms for WaitToKillServiceTimeout where this entry uses 2000 ms; neither figure is verifiable, so the value was left unchanged.
tweaks.notes: The shutdown and hang timeout values (revi.cc: 1500 ms service, 2000 ms app and hang) appear in no file of the ReviOS playbook source, so they are unverified. WaitToKillServiceTimeout is left at 2000 ms rather than rewritten to another unverified number.

tweaks.description: Disable Game DVR background recording.
tweaks.measuredEffect: Laptopmedia (GTA V, MX150 laptop): about 0.3 FPS difference while recording, within run noise.
tweaks.explanation: Turns off Game DVR background recording and the Game Bar capture hooks. The measured FPS cost of recording is tiny, so the gain is small, mostly on weak PCs.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Low-end or budget systems, and anyone who never uses Xbox Game Bar clips
tweaks.tradeoff: You lose Win+Alt+R clip capture and Game Bar recording. Fast, safe and easily reversed.

tweaks.description: Block UWP background apps.
tweaks.breaks: Alarms/mail/live tiles stop in background
tweaks.measuredEffect: Debloat-tool tests saved at most 100-200 MB RAM in total. Windows 10 Game Mode tests: about +6 fps only under heavy background load, 0-1 fps on clean systems. One guide reports 187 to 141 background processes combined with many other changes.
tweaks.explanation: Stops Store apps from running in the background when you are not using them. Helps most on PCs with many Store apps installed.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Laptops and low-RAM PCs with many Store apps
tweaks.tradeoff: Live tiles, notifications and mail/calendar sync from Store apps may be delayed.

tweaks.description: Stop Explorer folder-type auto detection.
tweaks.breaks: Clearing Bags/BagMRU loses per-folder view customisations (back up first)
tweaks.explanation: Stops Explorer from scanning folder contents to pick a view. In folders with very many files this can cut the delay when a folder first opens.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone with huge folders that open slowly in Explorer
tweaks.tradeoff: Folders may not pick the best view automatically, so you set views by hand.

tweaks.description: Disable Fault Tolerant Heap.
tweaks.breaks: No automatic heap shims for crashing apps
tweaks.explanation: Disables a feature that applies fixes to apps that keep crashing. It does not raise FPS and removes a stability helper.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Almost no one
tweaks.tradeoff: Crashing apps no longer get automatic mitigation.

tweaks.description: Disable Sleep Study diagnostic logs.
tweaks.explanation: Disable Sleep Study diagnostic logs.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who want to fine-tune Windows behaviour
tweaks.tradeoff: None documented.
tweaks.notes: In ReviOS the Sleep Study switch sits in the Revision Tool "Usage Reporting" toggle (with DPS and diagsvc), not in the default playbook. Native handler: one plan row per event channel; the snapshot keeps each channel's own enabled state, so undo does not turn on a channel that was already off. Nothing here touches the DPS or diagsvc services.

tweaks.description: Disable Reserved Storage (~7 GB).
tweaks.breaks: Feature updates may fail on low disk space
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured; catalog note: Frees about 7 GB disk
tweaks.explanation: Disable Reserved Storage (~7 GB).
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who want to fine-tune Windows behaviour
tweaks.tradeoff: Feature updates may fail on low disk space
tweaks.managedSkip: Reserved storage keeps feature updates from failing on a full disk; update reliability is IT's area.
tweaks.notes: Native handler: reads the state from 'DISM /Online /Get-ReservedStorageState' (ShippedWithReserves as a fallback), writes it with /Set-ReservedStorageState, and undo restores the recorded state. DISM refuses to change it while reserved storage is in use by a pending update, so the plan skips it while a restart or servicing is pending. The engine shows free disk space before and after.

tweaks.description: Disable Storage Sense auto-cleanup.
tweaks.breaks: Temp/Recycle Bin not auto-purged
tweaks.explanation: Turns off Storage Sense, which automatically deletes temp files and old Recycle Bin items. By default Storage Sense only runs when disk space is low, so turning it off has no performance benefit and removes the low-disk cleanup.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who want to fine-tune Windows behaviour
tweaks.tradeoff: Temp files and the Recycle Bin are no longer cleaned automatically, so disk space is freed less often.

tweaks.description: Delete user and system temp files (best effort).
tweaks.breaks: Running installers or updates can fail if their working files are deleted.
tweaks.explanation: Deletes everything in your temp folder and in C:\Windows\Temp. It frees disk space, but files cannot be restored.
tweaks.whoBenefits: People who want to reclaim a little disk space
tweaks.tradeoff: Not reversible. Can remove in-flight installer or Intune Management Extension working files, and files an open program still needs.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Can disturb app installs or Intune Management Extension runs that are in progress.

tweaks.description: Component store cleanup with /ResetBase (aggressive; disk-component-cleanup is the same cleanup without ResetBase).
tweaks.breaks: Microsoft: "All existing update packages can't be uninstalled" after /ResetBase. Fails with 0x800F0806 when servicing is pending.
tweaks.explanation: Component store cleanup with /ResetBase.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who want to fine-tune Windows behaviour
tweaks.tradeoff: Microsoft: after /ResetBase "All existing update packages can't be uninstalled." No native handler: the engine does not run this one (catalog strings are never executed); disk-component-cleanup is the supported variant.
tweaks.notes: Post-install possible with DISM /Online. tiny11's legacy script uses /ResetBase; its newer WinUI builder dropped it for the serviceable preset. The plain /StartComponentCleanup (no ResetBase) is now disk-component-cleanup. Measure first: Windows already runs a component cleanup task with a 30-day grace period.

tweaks.description: Component store cleanup (DISM /StartComponentCleanup, without /ResetBase).
tweaks.breaks: Superseded component versions are deleted for good, so a rollback to those exact versions is no longer possible; installed updates stay uninstallable (no /ResetBase). Fails with 0x800F0806 while servicing is pending.
tweaks.ram_or_perf_effect: Frees roughly 1-4.5 GB of disk, often less
tweaks.measuredEffect: Secondhand reports: about 1.16 GB (Elevenforum) to 4.5 GB (WOSHub) reclaimed; Windows already runs this cleanup in a scheduled task with a 30-day grace period, so the gain is often modest. The engine records 'AnalyzeComponentStore' size and free disk space before and after in the run log.
tweaks.explanation: Removes superseded versions of Windows components from the component store (WinSxS). This is the cleanup Windows itself schedules, run now, and it keeps every installed update uninstallable.
tweaks.whoBenefits: PCs that are short of system-drive space and have not run the scheduled cleanup recently
tweaks.tradeoff: No exact undo: the removed component versions are gone. Not in the safe preset and only runs with -AllowIrreversible. Can take several minutes.
tweaks.notes: Native handler (irreversible). The plan skips it without -AllowIrreversible and while a restart or servicing is pending. The analysis (DISM /AnalyzeComponentStore, about a minute) runs before and after the cleanup, never during -List. It never passes /ResetBase; that stays in perf-dism-cleanup-resetbase (aggressive).

tweaks.description: Legacy F8 boot menu policy.

implementation.undo: bcdedit /set {current} bootmenupolicy <recorded prior value, or /deletevalue when there was none>

tweaks.revert: bcdedit /set {current} bootmenupolicy <recorded prior value, or /deletevalue when there was none>
tweaks.explanation: Legacy F8 boot menu policy.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who want to fine-tune Windows behaviour
tweaks.tradeoff: None documented. A boot configuration change can make firmware ask for the BitLocker recovery key on some systems.
tweaks.notes: Native handler on the current boot entry. The plan skips it when BitLocker protection is on (or cannot be read), so it never triggers a recovery prompt. Undo restores the recorded value, or deletes the element when the entry had none.

tweaks.description: Disable peer-to-peer Delivery Optimization (0 HTTP only; 99 simple also acceptable).
tweaks.measuredEffect: 2Pint 25-client enterprise LAN test: default DO moved 26 GB, basic tuning 14 GB, tuned plus DNS-SD 11 GB over 4 hours (download side, forced updates). Measures an enterprise LAN, not a home PC; no consumer upload measurement exists.
tweaks.explanation: Stops your PC from sharing update files with other PCs on the internet. This is one of the few tweaks with a documented effect on bandwidth, mainly your upload.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Home users on slow or capped upstream links; metered connections
tweaks.tradeoff: Microsoft says turning DO off does not stop downloads. On a LAN, peering can reduce WAN traffic, so mode 0 can raise it. Mode 100 is deprecated and can cause error 0x80d03002.
tweaks.managedSkip: Delivery Optimization is configured by Intune (peering, Connected Cache); a local policy would conflict with it.

tweaks.description: Sync W32Time from pool.ntp.org (skip on domain-joined).
tweaks.breaks: Do not apply on domain-joined machines
tweaks.explanation: Points the Windows clock at pool.ntp.org instead of the default Microsoft time server.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users with specific network needs
tweaks.tradeoff: Do not use on domain-joined machines. The engine always skips this on managed devices because time sync is controlled by organisation policy.
tweaks.managedSkip: Time sync is owned by the organisation (domain / Entra time source).

tweaks.description: Disable IPv6 components.
tweaks.breaks: Some VPNs, Xbox networking; Microsoft advises against
tweaks.explanation: Disable IPv6 components.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users with specific network needs
tweaks.tradeoff: Some VPNs, Xbox networking; Microsoft advises against

tweaks.description: Disable Teredo.
tweaks.breaks: Some Xbox features, DO peering
tweaks.explanation: Disable Teredo.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users with specific network needs
tweaks.tradeoff: Some Xbox features, DO peering

tweaks.description: Disable NCSI active probe.
tweaks.breaks: Captive portal detection misreports
tweaks.measuredEffect: Single small HTTP GET per network change event
tweaks.explanation: Stops the small web check Windows uses to decide whether you are online. That probe is a tiny request, so the saving is negligible.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Isolated networks or privacy purists
tweaks.tradeoff: Windows may show 'no internet' and some apps misbehave.

tweaks.description: Stop automatic maps data download.
tweaks.explanation: Stops automatic download of offline maps. Documented by Microsoft and harmless, but it only matters if you have downloaded maps.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Metered or slow connections with offline maps installed
tweaks.tradeoff: Offline maps in the Maps app stay out of date. Do not disable the MapsBroker service instead.

tweaks.description: Prevent device metadata retrieval from network.
tweaks.explanation: Stops Windows from downloading device icons and descriptions from the internet when you plug in hardware.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users with specific network needs
tweaks.tradeoff: New hardware may show a generic name or icon in Devices and Printers. Drivers still install normally.

tweaks.description: Restrict anonymous SAM/share enumeration.
tweaks.explanation: Stops anonymous (not signed-in) network users from listing account names and shares on this PC. A standard hardening setting.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users with specific network needs
tweaks.tradeoff: Old tools and some legacy devices that browse shares anonymously stop being able to list them. Signed-in access is unaffected.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Often already set by a security baseline or Group Policy; the two values here may be overwritten at the next policy refresh.

tweaks.description: Disable SMB client bandwidth throttling (command step; skipped by the engine).
tweaks.explanation: Turns off the SMB client bandwidth throttle. This catalog entry is reference only: the engine never runs free-form commands, so it is skipped.
tweaks.whoBenefits: People who copy large files over SMB on fast LANs
tweaks.tradeoff: Higher peak load on the network from SMB transfers.

tweaks.description: Disable Recall / AI data analysis snapshots by policy (+ optional feature).
tweaks.ram_or_perf_effect: Avoids snapshot disk/CPU use on Copilot+ PCs
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured; no CPU/RAM/disk numbers found. Qualitative reports only (early Insider build felt slow).
tweaks.explanation: Turns off Recall, which takes periodic screenshots of your screen. The policy stops snapshots being saved and deletes ones already saved. The main win is privacy, not speed.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone on a Copilot+ PC or 24H2 Pro/Enterprise who does not want a searchable screen history on disk
tweaks.tradeoff: You lose the Recall timeline. Policy needs 24H2 with KB5055627 or later. Microsoft's page is inconsistent about Recall's default on managed devices, so check the result.

tweaks.description: Disable Windows Copilot by policy and hide the taskbar button (registry only, fully reversible).
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured; Microsoft says TurnOffWindowsCopilot does not control the newer Copilot app (24H2 and later)
tweaks.explanation: Sets the old Windows Copilot policy and hides the Copilot taskbar button. Microsoft marks TurnOffWindowsCopilot as deprecated and says it does not cover the newer Copilot app, so on 24H2 and later only the taskbar button change is reliably visible. App removal is a separate, irreversible tweak (ai-copilot-app-remove).
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who does not use Copilot and wants a cleaner taskbar
tweaks.tradeoff: The policy may do nothing on current builds; the taskbar button is hidden but the Copilot app stays installed. Microsoft: the TurnOffWindowsCopilot policy is subject to near-term deprecation; AppLocker is the documented replacement.

tweaks.description: Remove the Copilot app packages (no exact undo).

steps.how: winget/Store, or Add-AppxPackage -Register saved InstallLocation manifest

tweaks.measuredEffect: press measurement (Windows Latest, 2026-04): new Copilot app about 500 MB in background, about 1 GB active; previous native app under 100 MB
tweaks.explanation: Removes the Copilot app packages for all users and from the provisioning list. The engine skips AppX steps unless -AllowIrreversible is passed.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who never uses Copilot
tweaks.tradeoff: No exact undo: reinstall from the Microsoft Store. Updates or the Store can bring the app back.

tweaks.description: Disable Click to Do.
tweaks.explanation: Disables Click to Do, the overlay that lets you act on text or images on screen. It only runs on demand, so this mainly removes an entry point and AI features you did not ask for.
tweaks.whoBenefits: People who want fewer AI hooks in the shell
tweaks.tradeoff: Insider-only per Microsoft Learn; no effect on release builds until it ships. Support depends on your build.

tweaks.description: Uninstall OneDrive (only when no account configured; undo Known Folder Move first).
tweaks.breaks: Desktop/Documents redirection left pointing at OneDrive; data loss risk
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured; one process, roughly tens of MB when idle
tweaks.explanation: Removes OneDrive if you do not use it. Saves a small background process and stops the sign-in nags.
tweaks.whoBenefits: People with no OneDrive account
tweaks.tradeoff: If Desktop/Documents are backed up to OneDrive, uninstalling can strand files. Some guides advise leaving it alone.

tweaks.description: Disable OneDrive file sync by policy.
tweaks.breaks: Sync and Known Folder Backup stop
tweaks.explanation: Blocks OneDrive file sync by policy. Stops sync traffic but OneDrive stays installed.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Managed or offline-only PCs
tweaks.tradeoff: Cloud backup and Files On-Demand stop working.

tweaks.description: Block consumer Teams auto-install.
tweaks.measuredEffect: Teams plus Widgets about 0.5-1.0 GB on one low-end laptop (single machine). Microsoft documents the setting for setup time only.
tweaks.explanation: Stops the consumer Teams app from installing itself and starting at login. Teams can launch WebView2 processes at sign-in. Saves nothing if it is already installed.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Home users who do not use Teams, and low-RAM PCs
tweaks.tradeoff: Consumer Teams must be installed manually later. Little effect on an already-installed image; Microsoft documents no runtime policy for this on Pro.

tweaks.description: Remove WordPad, Steps Recorder, Math Recognizer and legacy Media Player (Windows capabilities), and disable the Internet Explorer and legacy Media Player optional features.
tweaks.revert: Snapshot per step: -Undo runs Add-WindowsCapability for each removed capability (needs Windows Update or Features on Demand access; the plan says when WSUS is configured without a repair source) and Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature for each disabled feature (the payload stays on disk, so no download).
tweaks.explanation: Remove WordPad, Steps Recorder, Math Recognizer and legacy Media Player (Windows capabilities), and disable the Internet Explorer and legacy Media Player optional features. Each step reads its own state first and is skipped when the component is not present on this edition or build (for example on LTSC). Language features and Defender are never touched.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who do not use the component
tweaks.tradeoff: Capabilities come back only with access to Windows Update or Features on Demand media. Disabled features come back offline.

tweaks.description: Force-remove Edge via external tool (EdgeRemover/--force-uninstall); fragile, unsupported outside EEA.
tweaks.breaks: WebView2 apps, Widgets, Search, Office features; Windows Update may reinstall
tweaks.explanation: Force-removes Edge. The Edge background processes are better handled by policies, and removal is fragile.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Almost nobody
tweaks.tradeoff: Unsupported, can break WebView2 apps, Widgets and Help. Win11Debloat authors also advise against it.

tweaks.description: Disable Store apps / auto-download.
tweaks.breaks: App installs and updates
tweaks.explanation: Disables the Store and its auto-downloads. Microsoft states this also stops app updates and the Store itself, a big functional cost for little traffic saved.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Locked-down kiosks
tweaks.tradeoff: Breaks the Store and app updates.

tweaks.description: Edge policy debloat: sidebar, shopping assistant, startup boost, background mode, metrics, personalization reporting.
tweaks.measuredEffect: Policies are documented by Microsoft but no memory figure is given; a third-party guide estimates hundreds of MB for Startup Boost while Edge is closed (unmeasured).
tweaks.explanation: Uses documented Edge policies to hide the sidebar and Copilot button, stop the shopping assistant, stop Edge pre-loading at sign-in (Startup Boost) and stop it staying alive after you close it (background mode).
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone with Edge installed, especially on 8 GB machines
tweaks.tradeoff: Edge opens a little slower from cold. Background sessions and push notifications from web apps stop when Edge is closed. Sidebar tools are lost.

tweaks.description: Edge privacy policies: no search suggestions/autofill, DNT, hide first run.
tweaks.explanation: Edge privacy policies: no search suggestions/autofill, DNT, hide first run.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Edge users with specific preferences
tweaks.tradeoff: None documented.

tweaks.description: Disable Edge password manager.
tweaks.explanation: Disable Edge password manager.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Edge users with specific preferences
tweaks.tradeoff: None documented.

tweaks.description: Disable Edge SmartScreen.
tweaks.explanation: Disable Edge SmartScreen.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Edge users with specific preferences
tweaks.tradeoff: None documented.

tweaks.description: Remove consumer AppX apps with the keep-work keep profile (exact names, reinstall manifest saved in the snapshot, framework check afterwards).
tweaks.revert: not reversible automatically: -Undo prints the reinstall manifest (winget / Store ids) from the snapshot; nothing is downloaded by the engine.
tweaks.breaks: Removes consumer apps; keeps Teams, Outlook, Terminal, Paint, Snipping Tool, Camera, Calculator, Notepad.
tweaks.explanation: Removes the packages in appx-profiles.json profile "keep-work" except the ones that profile keeps. Packages that are protected (Store, App Installer, VCLibs, UI.Xaml, WindowsAppRuntime, WebView2, Windows Security, shell components) are never matched, Teams and Outlook are kept on managed devices, and a check afterwards confirms the frameworks are still registered. Needs -AllowIrreversible.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Work PCs where the company apps must stay
tweaks.tradeoff: Removed apps come back only from the Microsoft Store or winget (feature updates may restore some).

tweaks.description: Remove consumer AppX apps with the keep-personal keep profile (exact names, reinstall manifest saved in the snapshot, framework check afterwards).
tweaks.revert: not reversible automatically: -Undo prints the reinstall manifest (winget / Store ids) from the snapshot; nothing is downloaded by the engine.
tweaks.breaks: Removes promo apps, Teams and Outlook; keeps everyday tools, Phone Link and Media Player.
tweaks.explanation: Removes the packages in appx-profiles.json profile "keep-personal" except the ones that profile keeps. Packages that are protected (Store, App Installer, VCLibs, UI.Xaml, WindowsAppRuntime, WebView2, Windows Security, shell components) are never matched, Teams and Outlook are kept on managed devices, and a check afterwards confirms the frameworks are still registered. Needs -AllowIrreversible.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Personal PCs
tweaks.tradeoff: Removed apps come back only from the Microsoft Store or winget (feature updates may restore some).

tweaks.description: Remove consumer AppX apps with the minimal keep profile (exact names, reinstall manifest saved in the snapshot, framework check afterwards).
tweaks.revert: not reversible automatically: -Undo prints the reinstall manifest (winget / Store ids) from the snapshot; nothing is downloaded by the engine.
tweaks.breaks: Keeps only Calculator, Notepad, Photos, Snipping Tool and Terminal.
tweaks.explanation: Removes the packages in appx-profiles.json profile "minimal" except the ones that profile keeps. Packages that are protected (Store, App Installer, VCLibs, UI.Xaml, WindowsAppRuntime, WebView2, Windows Security, shell components) are never matched, Teams and Outlook are kept on managed devices, and a check afterwards confirms the frameworks are still registered. Needs -AllowIrreversible.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who want the smallest app set
tweaks.tradeoff: Removed apps come back only from the Microsoft Store or winget (feature updates may restore some).

tweaks.description: Remove consumer/promo AppX + provisioned copies (allowlist; never Store, App Installer, Security, shell, runtimes).

revert.how: winget/Store, or Add-AppxPackage -Register saved InstallLocation manifest

tweaks.breaks: Some apps return after updates; Atlas Deprovisioned keys may block reinstall (delete per-package key)
tweaks.ram_or_perf_effect: Mostly disk; Yahoo test found idle RAM barely changes
tweaks.explanation: Removes promotional and consumer apps from the machine and the provisioning list so they do not come back for new users. Mostly frees disk space and clutter, not speed.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Fresh installs and shared machines
tweaks.tradeoff: New Outlook is documented as impossible to block from installing on builds after 23H2, so it may return; use provisioned-package removal.

tweaks.description: Remove Widgets platform packages (policy Dsh AllowNewsAndInterests=0 is the reversible alternative).

tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who do not pair a phone
tweaks.tradeoff: Lose Phone Link, notification mirroring and file transfer to the phone. Reinstallable from the Store.

tweaks.description: Restore Windows 10 right-click menu (restart Explorer).
tweaks.explanation: Brings back the full Windows 10 right-click menu so you do not have to click Show more options. Saves a click; some people find it opens faster, but there is no measurement.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Power users who use right-click actions often
tweaks.tradeoff: Overrides the new compact menu, and a future update may change it. Needs an Explorer restart.

tweaks.description: Dark mode, transparency off (cosmetic).
tweaks.measuredEffect: DWM composition adds roughly one frame of latency (author's own estimate); the original 8 ms vs 17 ms figures were largely retracted in a 2020 update
tweaks.explanation: Switches Windows and apps to the dark theme and turns off transparency effects. Cosmetic: the claimed latency benefit was largely retracted by its author, so no speed gain is claimed.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Low-end or integrated GPU systems, or people who prefer the look
tweaks.tradeoff: Loses the translucent look of Start, the taskbar and Settings; changes the look of every app that follows the system theme.

tweaks.description: Add End Task to taskbar menu.
tweaks.explanation: Adds an End task option to the taskbar right-click menu so you can close a frozen app quickly. Does not speed anything up but makes recovery from hangs faster.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who often deals with frozen apps
tweaks.tradeoff: A quick way to kill an app can discard unsaved work.

tweaks.description: Disable 5x-Shift Sticky Keys popup.
tweaks.explanation: Stops the Sticky Keys prompt when you tap Shift five times. A pure annoyance fix, useful for gamers.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Gamers and fast typists
tweaks.tradeoff: Loses the shortcut for people who rely on Sticky Keys for accessibility.

tweaks.description: Show file extensions.
tweaks.explanation: Shows file extensions like .exe and .pdf. A safety and clarity tweak, not a speed one; helps spot disguised files.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Everyone, especially for spotting fake file types
tweaks.tradeoff: None meaningful.

tweaks.description: Disable Windows Chat icon and Widgets (policy).
tweaks.measuredEffect: One author's laptop: roughly 0.5-1.0 GB extra memory with default Teams and Widgets. Controlled debloat test: at most 100-200 MB saved overall. Conflict noted; Microsoft gives no figure.
tweaks.explanation: Turns off Widgets and the Chat icon with Microsoft's supported policy. Widgets stops running its background processes and news feed. A clean, reversible, supported way to do it.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Low-RAM PCs (under 8 GB) and anyone who does not use Widgets
tweaks.tradeoff: No weather or news panel. The Chat icon policy is Enterprise/Education only. The Windows Feeds EnableFeeds value is Windows 10 only; the Dsh AllowNewsAndInterests part does the work.

tweaks.description: Remove 'Edit with Paint 3D' context entries.

implementation.run: foreach($e in '.3mf','.bmp','.fbx','.gif','.jfif','.jpe','.jpeg','.jpg','.png','.tif','.tiff'){reg export then reg delete HKCR\SystemFileAssociations\$e\Shell\3D Edit}

tweaks.explanation: Removes the Edit with Paint 3D entry from the right-click menu of image files.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who want a tidier interface
tweaks.tradeoff: The menu entry disappears (the Paint 3D app stays installed) and an update may bring it back. The engine currently skips this entry because it is a command step.

tweaks.description: Defer feature updates 30-365 days; quality/security updates keep flowing.
tweaks.breaks: Update-ring settings from Intune or Group Policy can be overridden or can override this.
tweaks.explanation: Delays feature updates (the yearly Windows version upgrades) by 30 days using the Windows Update policy keys. Monthly security and quality updates are not delayed.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who need control over update timing
tweaks.tradeoff: Conflicts with Intune/WUfB update rings or Autopatch; feature updates arrive 30 days late.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Conflicts with Intune update rings / Windows Autopatch; the engine already skips the updates category on managed devices.
tweaks.managedSkip: Windows Update settings are owned by the organisation (Intune update rings, WUfB, Autopatch).

tweaks.description: Disable VBS / Memory Integrity / Credential Guard (reboot). Windows may re-enable from Oct 2026.
tweaks.breaks: Loses kernel code-integrity and driver defences
tweaks.ram_or_perf_effect: 0% on Cinebench, roughly 7-15% on some older gaming PCs (secondhand)
tweaks.measuredEffect: ComputerBase (Nov 2023, Win11 22H2): HVCI on/off can mean double-digit differences in CPU-limited scenes. Tom's Hardware (secondhand): about 5-7% average, up to 15% 1% lows with VBS on in 12th-gen tests; worst cases about 30% on older CPUs without MBEC.
tweaks.explanation: Memory Integrity (HVCI) runs a security layer under Windows using virtualization. It can cost frame rate in CPU-limited games, mostly on older processors. It has a real measured effect, but switches off a significant protection.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Owners of older CPUs or high-refresh CPU-bound esports setups who measured a gain on their own games
tweaks.tradeoff: Removes kernel code-integrity and driver protections. Windows may turn it back on. Test your own games and keep it on for a general-use PC.

tweaks.description: Disable CPU/OS exploit mitigations.
tweaks.explanation: Turns off CPU exploit mitigations such as those for Spectre-class flaws. No gaming benchmark was found, and modern CPUs have hardware fixes, so the gain is small.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Almost no one; only very old CPUs might see a gain
tweaks.tradeoff: Exposes the system to known CPU side-channel attacks. Not recommended.

tweaks.description: EnableLinkedConnections for mapped drives under elevation.
tweaks.breaks: Weaker UAC isolation.
tweaks.explanation: Makes mapped network drives visible to both elevated and non-elevated processes by linking the two access tokens. That weakens the isolation UAC provides.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Admins who need mapped drives to show up in elevated prompts
tweaks.tradeoff: Weakens UAC token isolation: a non-elevated program can see what an elevated one maps.

tweaks.description: Execution policy RemoteSigned (LocalMachine). Relaxes the Windows client default.
tweaks.breaks: Weaker defence against malicious local scripts.
tweaks.explanation: Changes the PowerShell execution policy for the whole machine to RemoteSigned, so unsigned local scripts can run. The Windows 11 client default is Restricted. This is a convenience for script authors, not a performance tweak.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Developers and admins who run their own unsigned scripts; not a general recommendation
tweaks.tradeoff: Weakens the script execution policy: any local unsigned script can run. On managed devices policy from Intune, AppLocker or WDAC normally controls this.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Conflicts with execution-policy settings pushed by Intune or Group Policy.
