tweaks.description: Enable inline sudo (24H2+).
tweaks.explanation: Enable inline sudo (24H2+).
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users with a specific need
tweaks.tradeoff: None documented.

tweaks.description: Disable SysMain (Superfetch) service.
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured on SSD/NVMe; the only pro-disable report (Tech Community) counts standby cache as used RAM. Engadget and HelpDeskGeek: only worth trying on HDD or under 4 GB RAM.
tweaks.explanation: SysMain pre-loads frequently used apps into memory. It was designed for slow hard drives and does little on SSD or NVMe drives. The only report of a gain counts standby memory as used, but standby memory is free memory: Windows hands it to apps on demand, so a high figure there is not a problem. Engadget and HelpDeskGeek advise leaving SysMain on except on an HDD or under 4 GB of RAM.
tweaks.whoBenefits: SSD/NVMe users who want fewer background disk reads; not HDD users
tweaks.tradeoff: On a hard drive, app launches and boot can get slower.

tweaks.description: Set Windows Search (WSearch) to Manual instead of Automatic.
tweaks.measuredEffect: one reviewer: nearly 1 GB on a 16 GB laptop (single machine, unrepeated); Microsoft: normal is a few hundred MB. Microsoft KB 4558579: typical index under 30,000 items, issues above 400,000; GB-level indexer memory points to a corrupted index (rebuild).
tweaks.explanation: The Windows Search indexer can use a lot of memory when its index is large or corrupted; one reviewer reported over 1 GB freed, though Microsoft says a few hundred MB is normal. Microsoft favours rebuilding the index over disabling. Manual start is gentler than Disabled.
tweaks.whoBenefits: People with a huge or broken index who use a separate search tool; first try rebuilding the index
tweaks.tradeoff: Slower Start/Explorer search, Outlook search may degrade, and server-side search for SMB shares depends on it.

tweaks.description: Disable the Print Spooler service on PCs that never print.
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured for RAM; security benefit documented by Microsoft
tweaks.explanation: Mainly a security hardening step: the Print Spooler has been a repeated attack target, and Microsoft recommends disabling it on domain controllers and admin systems. It saves almost no memory. Do not use if you print, including to PDF printers that rely on the spooler.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Non-printing PCs, domain controllers, admin workstations
tweaks.tradeoff: No local or remote printing; check dependencies first.

tweaks.description: Keep Remote Registry disabled.
tweaks.breaks: Remote management, inventory and monitoring tools that read the registry remotely (for example some ConfigMgr and RMM tools).
tweaks.explanation: Remote Registry lets other machines read your registry over the network. It is a security hardening item (it appears in CIS benchmarks), not a performance one, and it is disabled by default on most client installs. Remote management tools such as Configuration Manager need it.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Home PCs and hardened machines; not managed fleets
tweaks.tradeoff: Breaks remote management tools that use the remote registry.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Remote management or inventory tools used by your IT team may stop working.
tweaks.managedSkip: Remote inventory and monitoring tools (ConfigMgr, RMM) read the registry remotely.

tweaks.description: Disable Downloaded Maps Manager (MapsBroker).
tweaks.explanation: Handles offline map downloads for the Maps app. It is idle unless you use offline maps, so there is no real gain, but it is listed in CIS hardening.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Hardening-minded users
tweaks.tradeoff: Offline Maps stop updating.

tweaks.description: Restore system-wide timer resolution requests (GlobalTimerResolutionRequests=1) so one app's high-resolution timer request applies to all processes, as before Windows 10 2004.
tweaks.breaks: Battery life on laptops; slightly higher idle power on desktops.
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured; tools such as MeasureSleep show Sleep() precision changes, but no input-lag or frame-time benefit was documented
tweaks.explanation: Since Windows 10 2004 only the program that asks for a faster timer gets it; other programs stay at about 15.6 ms. This value makes requests system-wide again. Microsoft says higher resolution can reduce overall performance, use more power and block CPU power saving. No instrumented before/after latency numbers were found.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who run a timer-sensitive app and depend on other processes seeing the fast timer; mostly audio or legacy-software cases
tweaks.tradeoff: More CPU wakeups, higher idle power and battery drain, and possibly lower throughput.

tweaks.description: Turn off per-user Game DVR app capture and background (historical) recording.
tweaks.measuredEffect: Laptopmedia: about 0.3 FPS difference, within noise (GTA V, MX150).
tweaks.explanation: Switches off Game Bar app capture and the always-on background recording buffer for your account only. Measured cost of recording is about 0.3 FPS on a weak laptop, so expect a small gain mainly on low-end PCs.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Budget or older PCs that never use Game Bar clips
tweaks.tradeoff: No Win+Alt+G background clips; Game Bar recording features stop working.

tweaks.description: Turn off all Windows Spotlight features (lock screen Spotlight, tips and suggestions) for the current user by policy.
tweaks.explanation: Microsoft documents this policy as the switch that turns off every Windows Spotlight feature, including lock-screen ads and tips, for a user. It is about a quieter, ad-free screen and a bit less network traffic, not speed.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who wants the lock screen and Settings free of promotions and rotating suggestions; metered links
tweaks.tradeoff: The lock screen falls back to a picture or slideshow. Microsoft's table shows the matching policy as not supported on Pro, and it does not cover per-user Settings toggles, so the effect may be limited there.

tweaks.description: Cap Delivery Optimization monthly upload to 5 GB instead of the 20 GB default, keeping peering but bounding upstream use.
tweaks.measuredEffect: No measurement found (the 20 GB figure is Microsoft's default cap, not a measured effect).
tweaks.explanation: Limits how much your PC may upload to other PCs per month (5 GB instead of the 20 GB default). Redundant if net-delivery-optimization-off is applied: with DODownloadMode=0 there is no peering, so there is nothing to cap.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Home users on capped or slow upstream connections.
tweaks.tradeoff: Peers get fewer shares from your PC once the cap is reached. Pointless if peer-to-peer is already off.
tweaks.managedSkip: Delivery Optimization is configured by Intune (peering, Connected Cache); a local policy would conflict with it.

tweaks.description: Limit Delivery Optimization background downloads to 25 percent of measured bandwidth (default is dynamic, up to 45 percent).
tweaks.explanation: Keeps background update downloads from using most of your connection. Microsoft says throttling is the supported way to reduce DO network load, as turning DO off does not stop downloads.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who notice lag during background updates.
tweaks.tradeoff: Background updates download more slowly.
tweaks.managedSkip: Delivery Optimization is configured by Intune (peering, Connected Cache); a local policy would conflict with it.

tweaks.description: Stop the Maps settings page from generating untriggered network traffic.
tweaks.explanation: Documented by Microsoft as the companion to the automatic map update policy. It prevents map traffic when you merely open the Settings page.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users.
tweaks.tradeoff: None meaningful; Maps keeps working.

tweaks.description: Hide the Recommended section of the Start menu (recent files and suggested items) using the documented Start policy.
tweaks.explanation: Removes the Recommended area of Start, where Windows shows recent files and suggested apps and sites. Documented by Microsoft as a policy from Windows 11 22H2, so it is the official route rather than a hack. A cleaner, less ad-prone Start, not a speed gain.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who wants a minimal Start menu.
tweaks.tradeoff: You lose quick access to recently opened files from Start. Reports differ on edition support; Microsoft's CSP table lists Pro.

tweaks.description: Disable Paint AI features (Cocreator, Generative Fill, Image Creator) by device policy.
tweaks.explanation: Switches off the AI image tools inside Paint while keeping Paint itself. These policies live in a separate Paint key, not the WindowsAI key.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who want Paint without cloud AI features.
tweaks.tradeoff: You lose Cocreator, Generative Fill and Image Creator. Needs a recent Paint and Windows update.

tweaks.description: Block AI features (Rewrite, summarise) in Notepad by policy.
tweaks.explanation: Notepad's AI text tools are on by default on managed devices. This policy blocks them. Microsoft's page names the policy DisableAIFeaturesInNotepad but gives the registry value as DisableAIFeatures, so test on one machine first.
tweaks.whoBenefits: People who want Notepad as a plain editor.
tweaks.tradeoff: You lose Rewrite and related AI helpers. The value name is inconsistent in the docs; verify the AI buttons disappear. Needs Notepad 11.2503.16.0 or later.

tweaks.description: Turn off lock screen widgets via the Dsh policy.
tweaks.explanation: Removes widgets such as weather from the lock screen. Microsoft labels this policy as Insider Preview, so it may not take effect on every build. The wider AllowNewsAndInterests=0 policy covers the whole Widgets experience.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users who want a clean lock screen.
tweaks.tradeoff: Insider-only per Microsoft Learn; no effect on release builds until it ships. No weather or widget info on the lock screen once it applies.

tweaks.description: Hide the Copilot Chat icon in the Edge toolbar (Entra ID profiles).
tweaks.explanation: Sets the documented Edge policy Microsoft365CopilotChatIconEnabled to 0, which hides the Copilot Chat icon (Edge 139 and later, Entra ID profiles only). Page-context handling is a separate tweak.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Edge users signed in with a work or school account.
tweaks.tradeoff: Only applies to Entra ID profiles. The icon is hidden; Copilot itself is not removed.

tweaks.description: Stop Edge Copilot reading page context for Entra ID users (also disables Microsoft 365 link auto-open in Copilot).
tweaks.breaks: Copilot page-context features for licensed Entra users.
tweaks.explanation: Sets EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext to 0. Besides stopping Copilot from reading the page you are on, Microsoft documents that this also turns off M365LinksAutoOpenCopilotEnabled, so Microsoft 365 links no longer open in Copilot, for licensed Entra users.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Organisations or users who do not want Copilot to read page content
tweaks.tradeoff: A functional change, not just hiding an icon: Copilot page summaries and Microsoft 365 link handoff stop working for Entra ID profiles.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Overrides an Edge policy your admin may have set; check edge://policy.

tweaks.description: Stop Outlook prompting users to migrate to the new Outlook.
tweaks.explanation: Disables the automatic migration to the new Outlook for Windows in classic Outlook. It does not stop the new Outlook app being preinstalled: Microsoft says that cannot be blocked on builds after 23H2.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Classic Outlook users.
tweaks.tradeoff: Only helps with classic Outlook; the new app remains installed.

tweaks.description: Lock Chrome Memory Saver on by policy (HighEfficiencyModeEnabled).
tweaks.measuredEffect: One independent test (Benchmark.pl, n=1): Chrome 1414 MB at start, about 7.5% lower after 40 min, about 83% lower after a long idle. Google claims up to 40% (vendor). Memory Saver is on by default in recent Chrome; the policy locks it on.
tweaks.explanation: Memory Saver discards background tabs after a period of inactivity, which frees their memory. Tabs that play audio or video, share the screen, have partly filled forms, run downloads or are pinned are kept.
tweaks.whoBenefits: People with many Chrome tabs open, such as 100+ processes on a 16-32 GB PC
tweaks.tradeoff: Discarded tabs reload when you switch back to them. Users cannot turn Memory Saver off while the policy is set; the savings level stays user-controlled.

tweaks.description: Set Chrome Memory Saver to the Maximum savings level (MemorySaverModeSavings = 2).
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured for the Maximum level; see chrome-memory-saver-on for the default level
tweaks.explanation: Turns Memory Saver on and sets the Maximum savings level, so background tabs go inactive sooner than at the Moderate default. Needs Chrome 126 or later. Pick this or chrome-memory-saver-on, not both.
tweaks.whoBenefits: People who still run short of memory with the default Memory Saver level
tweaks.tradeoff: Tabs go inactive sooner and reload more often, which costs network and time.

tweaks.description: Stop Chrome from running in the background after the last window is closed (BackgroundModeEnabled = 0).
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured; prevents Chrome processes staying resident after the last window closes
tweaks.explanation: By default Chrome can keep a background process alive after you close the last window so apps and extensions keep running. The policy turns that off, so closing Chrome ends its processes and frees their memory.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Chrome users who close the browser and expect its memory to be released
tweaks.tradeoff: Chrome apps and extensions that rely on running in the background (some notification and sync features) stop when Chrome is closed.

tweaks.description: Recommend Edge sleeping tabs on with a 5-minute timeout (user-overridable defaults).
tweaks.measuredEffect: Microsoft telemetry: about 39.1 MB saved per slept tab on average (6 billion tabs over 28 days); Edge 100 claim of 85% memory per slept tab. Default timeout is 900 s; this sets 300 s.
tweaks.explanation: Sleeping tabs are on by default. This sets a recommended (user-overridable) default and shortens the timeout from 15 to 5 minutes. Edge heuristics skip tabs that play audio, stream or show notifications.
tweaks.whoBenefits: People with many Edge tabs open in the background
tweaks.tradeoff: Idle tabs wake with a short delay. Does not apply to Edge profiles signed in with a personal Microsoft account (Learn: Applies to a profile that is signed in with a Microsoft account: No). On managed devices Intune may already set these.

tweaks.description: Cap Edge memory at 4 GB (TotalMemoryLimitMb = 4096, mandatory policy).
tweaks.measuredEffect: not measured; Microsoft: no guarantee the browser stays under the limit; without the policy Edge only saves memory when physical memory is low
tweaks.explanation: Sets a memory limit for the Edge browser. Once Edge passes the limit it discards tabs to get back under it. Only the mandatory path is supported; the Recommended path does not work for this policy.
tweaks.whoBenefits: PCs where Edge grows past several GB and crowds out other programs
tweaks.tradeoff: Tabs are discarded and fully reloaded once Edge passes 4 GB; heavy web apps may lose state.

tweaks.description: Make Windows Search respect the power mode and not index on battery.
tweaks.ram_or_perf_effect: Less background indexing CPU on battery
tweaks.explanation: Tells the Windows Search indexer to follow the active power mode (RespectPowerModes) and to skip indexing while the PC runs on battery (PreventIndexOnBattery policy).
tweaks.whoBenefits: Laptop users who see indexer CPU or battery drain
tweaks.tradeoff: New files are not searchable until the PC is back on mains power. Added from ReviOS research; not yet tested on a real Windows 11 25H2 machine.

tweaks.description: Limit diagnostic log and dump collection and hide the diagnostic data opt-in page.
tweaks.breaks: Support cases get less diagnostic data (logs, dumps); the diagnostic data page in Settings is hidden
tweaks.explanation: Three documented diagnostic-data policies that ReviOS sets: limit the diagnostic logs and crash dumps that can be collected, and hide the opt-in page in Settings.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users who do not need Microsoft or IT to collect logs
tweaks.tradeoff: On an Intune-managed device these reduce what IT can collect for troubleshooting, so the engine skips this tweak there.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Reduces the logs and dumps IT can pull for support cases; may conflict with the Intune diagnostics-data policy.
tweaks.managedSkip: Limits the diagnostic logs and dumps IT can collect for support.

tweaks.description: Run the Windows Search indexer at Below Normal CPU priority.
tweaks.breaks: Indexing finishes later on a busy PC
tweaks.explanation: Sets the PerfOptions CpuPriorityClass of SearchIndexer.exe to 5 (Below Normal), as ReviOS does. Only this one executable: ReviOS also lowers lsass, sihost, ctfmon and fontdrvhost, which DebloatKit deliberately does not copy (slow sign-in and Windows Hello, IME input lag).
tweaks.whoBenefits: Users whose PC stutters while the indexer runs
tweaks.tradeoff: A priority class is not a measured speed-up. Added from ReviOS research; not yet tested on a real machine. This is not an IFEO Debugger value.

tweaks.description: Skip the first sign-in animation of new accounts.
tweaks.explanation: Turns off the "Hi / We are getting things ready" animation the first time a new account signs in (policy EnableFirstLogonAnimation = 0).
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who creates new local accounts
tweaks.tradeoff: Affects only the first sign-in of new accounts. Cosmetic. Added from ReviOS research; not yet tested on a real Windows 11 25H2 machine.

tweaks.description: Disable the WAP Push Message Routing service (dmwappushservice).
tweaks.breaks: MDM push routing: an Intune-enrolled device can stop syncing on demand; some SMS / WAP features stop
tweaks.explanation: tiny11 sets this service to Disabled in the image. It routes WAP push messages that MDM uses to wake the device, so it is listed here mainly so the managed-device guard has a reason to refuse it.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Unmanaged PCs that never use MDM, push or SMS routing
tweaks.tradeoff: No measurable gain. Never apply on an Intune or other MDM-managed PC.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Breaks MDM push routing, so Intune can no longer nudge the device to sync.
tweaks.managedSkip: dmwappushservice routes MDM push messages; disabling it breaks Intune sync.

tweaks.description: Stop websites reading the Windows language list (HttpAcceptLanguageOptOut).
tweaks.explanation: Turns off "Let websites show me locally relevant content by accessing my language list" in Settings > Privacy > General. Websites and apps then see only the primary language, which removes a small fingerprinting signal. The per-user (HKCU) part applies to the user running the engine only.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users
tweaks.tradeoff: Sites that pick a language from the full list may fall back to the first language.

tweaks.description: Stop the "Let's finish setting up your device" screen (SCOOBE) after updates.
tweaks.explanation: Turns off Settings > System > Notifications > "Suggest ways to get the most out of Windows and finish setting up this device". This is the full-screen nag after feature updates that pushes Microsoft 365, OneDrive backup and Game Pass. The per-user (HKCU) part applies to the user running the engine only.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who is tired of the post-update setup screen
tweaks.tradeoff: None functional; you no longer get the setup reminders.

tweaks.description: Hide sync-provider notifications (OneDrive and Microsoft 365 promotions) in File Explorer.
tweaks.explanation: Turns off File Explorer > Options > View > "Show sync provider notifications", which is where the OneDrive storage and Microsoft 365 banners at the top of Explorer come from. OneDrive itself keeps syncing. The per-user (HKCU) part applies to the user running the engine only.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who sees OneDrive or Microsoft 365 banners in Explorer
tweaks.tradeoff: You also miss genuine sync-provider notices in Explorer (OneDrive still shows them in its own tray icon).

tweaks.description: Hide Microsoft account notifications (badges and prompts) on the Start menu.
tweaks.explanation: Turns off Settings > Personalization > Start > "Show account-related notifications": the badge on your profile picture in Start that pushes backup, Microsoft 365 or account completion. The per-user (HKCU) part applies to the user running the engine only.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who wants a quiet Start menu
tweaks.tradeoff: You may miss a real account warning (for example an expired password) in Start; Settings still shows it.

tweaks.description: Hide tips, shortcuts and new-app recommendations in Start (Start_IrisRecommendations).
tweaks.explanation: Turns off Settings > Personalization > Start > "Show recommendations for tips, shortcuts, new apps, and more". It is the user-level setting next to the HideRecommendedSection policy in start-hide-recommended-section, and it works on editions where that policy is not honoured. The per-user (HKCU) part applies to the user running the engine only.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who wants Start without promotions
tweaks.tradeoff: None functional. Recent files in Start are not affected by this value.

tweaks.description: Turn off search highlights (Bing trending content and doodles in the search box and Start search).
tweaks.explanation: Uses the documented "Allow search highlights" policy (EnableDynamicContentInWSB = 0) plus the matching user setting, so Windows Search stops loading trending web content and illustrations. Sophia sets only the user value and removes the policy; the policy is the more durable route on an unmanaged PC. It may already be off when priv-search-cortana-bing-off is applied. The per-user (HKCU) part applies to the user running the engine only.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users; anyone who finds the search box distracting
tweaks.tradeoff: No trending or daily content in search. Local search is unchanged.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Overrides a Search policy your admin may set; on a managed device the policy part can be replaced at the next sync.

tweaks.description: Stop F1 opening a Bing search in Edge ("How to get help in Windows").
tweaks.explanation: Registers an empty per-user override of the HelpPane type library, so pressing F1 on the desktop or in Explorer no longer launches Edge with a Bing "get help" search. F1 inside applications keeps working. Same technique as ui-classic-context-menu (a per-user class override). The per-user (HKCU) part applies to the user running the engine only.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who hits F1 by accident (laptops with Fn-row keys, gamers)
tweaks.tradeoff: The Windows F1 help shortcut is gone; use the Get Help app instead. A future update may change the HelpPane registration.

tweaks.description: Do not add "- Shortcut" to the name of new shortcuts.
tweaks.explanation: New shortcuts are named after their target without the " - Shortcut" suffix. Existing shortcuts keep their names. The per-user (HKCU) part applies to the user running the engine only.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who creates desktop shortcuts
tweaks.tradeoff: Shortcuts are harder to tell apart from the original by name alone (the arrow overlay stays).

tweaks.description: Remove "Look for an app in the Microsoft Store" from the Open with dialog.
tweaks.explanation: Applies the documented per-user policy "Turn off access to the Store" for the Open with dialog, so opening an unknown file type does not offer a Store search. The per-user (HKCU) part applies to the user running the engine only.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who opens unusual file types
tweaks.tradeoff: You find a handler app yourself instead of through the Store link. The Store itself still works.

tweaks.description: Stop the Game Bar showing its tips panel when a game starts.
tweaks.explanation: Hides the Game Bar startup panel ("Press Win+G to open Game Bar") at game launch. Sophia only applies it when the Xbox app is installed; writing the value without the app is harmless. The per-user (HKCU) part applies to the user running the engine only.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Gamers who keep Game Bar installed
tweaks.tradeoff: None functional.

tweaks.description: Import JPEG wallpapers at 100 % quality instead of re-compressing them.
tweaks.explanation: Windows re-encodes JPEG wallpapers at about 85 % quality, which shows as banding on gradients and large screens. 100 keeps the original quality. Applies the next time a wallpaper is set. The per-user (HKCU) part applies to the user running the engine only.
tweaks.whoBenefits: People with high-resolution or large monitors
tweaks.tradeoff: The cached wallpaper file is a few MB larger.

tweaks.description: Do not use AutoPlay for any media or device (per user).
tweaks.explanation: Turns off Settings > Bluetooth & devices > AutoPlay. Inserting a USB stick, phone or disc no longer pops up an action or starts one. A small hardening and annoyance fix; AutoRun from USB is already blocked by Windows. The per-user (HKCU) part applies to the user running the engine only.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who plugs in USB drives, cameras or phones
tweaks.tradeoff: No automatic import prompt for photos or media; open the device in Explorer instead.

tweaks.description: Stop Windows changing the default printer to the last one used.
tweaks.explanation: Turns off Settings > Printers & scanners > "Let Windows manage my default printer", so the default printer stays the one you chose, also after you print once to another printer or change network. The per-user (HKCU) part applies to the user running the engine only.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Office and home users with more than one printer (including PDF printers)
tweaks.tradeoff: Windows no longer picks a printer per network location for you.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Printer defaults may also be set by IT (Universal Print or Group Policy).

tweaks.description: Enable Win32 long path support (paths longer than 260 characters).
tweaks.explanation: The documented "Enable Win32 long paths" setting. Apps that declare longPathAware in their manifest (PowerShell 7, Git for Windows, Node, Python 3.6+, .NET apps) can then use paths beyond MAX_PATH. Apps that do not opt in are unaffected.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Developers (node_modules, deep repos), people syncing deep SharePoint/OneDrive folders
tweaks.tradeoff: None for normal use. Explorer and many older apps still stop at 260 characters, so a long path made by one tool may not open in another.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Often already set by IT for developers; the same value can be pushed by Intune or Group Policy.

tweaks.description: Show the stop-code parameters on the blue screen.
tweaks.explanation: Adds the four bug-check parameters to the stop screen, which helps diagnose a crash that does not leave a dump (for example when the pagefile is too small or the disk is the cause).
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone troubleshooting crashes; support staff
tweaks.tradeoff: None; only the crash screen changes.

tweaks.description: Keep the thumbnail cache when Disk Cleanup and maintenance run.
tweaks.ram_or_perf_effect: Avoids thumbnail regeneration after automatic cleanups; not measured
tweaks.explanation: Stops automatic maintenance (silent Disk Cleanup) from deleting thumbcache_*.db, so folders with many photos or videos do not rebuild their thumbnails after a cleanup. Manual Disk Cleanup can still clear it.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Photo and video folders, slower disks
tweaks.tradeoff: The thumbnail cache keeps its space (usually tens to a few hundred MB).

tweaks.description: Stop Edge updates creating desktop shortcuts (Stable, Beta, Dev, Canary).
tweaks.explanation: The documented Edge Update policy "Prevent Desktop Shortcut creation upon install" per channel. Edge stops putting its shortcut back on the desktop after each update. Edge keeps updating.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who deletes the Edge desktop shortcut
tweaks.tradeoff: None functional.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: Edge Update may be governed by Intune or Group Policy; check edge://policy.
tweaks.notes: Sophia function: PreventEdgeShortcutCreation -Channels Stable, Beta, Dev, Canary

tweaks.description: Disable more diagnostic and Maps tasks: MareBackup, Disk Diagnostic data collector, MapsToastTask, MapsUpdateTask.
tweaks.explanation: Completes task-telemetry-set with the tasks Sophia also disables: MareBackup (gathers Win32 app inventory for the App Backup scenario and runs the compatibility telemetry runner), the disk diagnostic data collector (uploads disk data for CEIP participants) and the two Maps tasks (map toasts and offline-map update checks). Tasks that are already disabled or absent on a build are left alone. On build 26200 the Disk Diagnostic and MapsUpdateTask tasks are already disabled by default.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Privacy-minded users; PCs without offline maps
tweaks.tradeoff: Windows Backup may not list desktop apps to restore on a new PC. Offline maps are not updated automatically (open Maps to update them).

tweaks.description: Receive updates for other Microsoft products (Microsoft Update) with Windows Update.
tweaks.explanation: Turns on Settings > Windows Update > Advanced options > "Receive updates for other Microsoft products". Windows Update then also patches products like Microsoft 365 MSI installs, Visual Studio components, SQL tools and older .NET runtimes. A security improvement, not a speed one.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Personal PCs with Microsoft software outside the Store
tweaks.tradeoff: Slightly more downloads during update checks.
tweaks.managedSkip: Windows Update settings are owned by the organisation (Intune update rings, WUfB, Autopatch).

tweaks.description: Notify me when a restart is required to finish updating.
tweaks.explanation: Turns on Settings > Windows Update > Advanced options > "Notify me when a restart is required to finish updating", so pending updates are visible instead of waiting silently for the next restart.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Anyone who postpones restarts
tweaks.tradeoff: An extra notification when an update is pending.
tweaks.managedSkip: Windows Update settings are owned by the organisation (Intune update rings, WUfB, Autopatch).

tweaks.description: Disable the Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser Exp scheduled task.
tweaks.breaks: Feature-update compatibility safeguard holds and readiness data built from the Appraiser.
tweaks.explanation: The experimental twin of the Compatibility Appraiser that some 24H2 builds ship. Same reasoning and same limits as task-compat-appraiser-off: it can cause CompatTelRunner bursts, and Windows uses its results for feature-update safeguards. Absent on this 26200 install, where the engine skips it as not present.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Low-end PCs with CompatTelRunner spikes that you update by hand
tweaks.tradeoff: Feature-update readiness and safeguard holds may work differently; Windows may re-enable the task.
tweaks.managedSkip: The Compatibility Appraiser feeds feature-update safeguard holds and Update Compliance / Autopatch readiness that IT relies on.
tweaks.managedDeviceImpact: The Appraiser feeds feature-update readiness and compatibility gating that Windows Update for Business / Autopatch rely on.

tweaks.description: Turn on PowerShell script block logging (event 4104).
tweaks.ram_or_perf_effect: Small extra event-log I/O while PowerShell runs
tweaks.explanation: Hardening, opt-in: the documented policy "Turn on PowerShell Script Block Logging" records the text of every PowerShell script block that runs in Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational, including deobfuscated code. It is what lets you or a security tool see afterwards what a malicious script did. Sophia also turns on module logging for all modules and process-creation auditing; those are left out here (module logging is very noisy, and process auditing needs auditpol, for which the engine has no handler).
tweaks.whoBenefits: Security-minded users and admins of unmanaged PCs
tweaks.tradeoff: More event-log writes when scripts run, and secrets that appear in script text (for example a password in a command line) end up in the event log. Windows already logs suspicious script blocks without this setting.
tweaks.managedSkip: PowerShell logging is part of the organisation's security baseline (Intune, Defender for Endpoint); a local policy can conflict with it.
tweaks.notes: Sophia function: EventViewerCustomView -Enable (script block part only)

tweaks.description: Run the Microsoft Defender Antivirus content scanner in a sandbox (MP_FORCE_USE_SANDBOX=1).
tweaks.ram_or_perf_effect: An extra sandboxed Defender process; memory cost not measured
tweaks.explanation: Hardening, opt-in: the machine environment variable Microsoft documents for running Defender's scanning in a low-privilege sandbox process, so a parser exploit in a scanned file does not run as SYSTEM. Takes effect after a restart. Has no effect when another antivirus product is active.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Personal PCs that use Defender as their antivirus
tweaks.tradeoff: An extra Defender process (MsMpEngCP.exe) and somewhat more memory. The environment variable is visible to every process.
tweaks.managedSkip: Defender configuration belongs to the organisation's security baseline.

tweaks.description: Do not use sign-in info to finish setting up the device after an update (turn off ARSO).
tweaks.explanation: The documented policy "Sign-in and lock last interactive user automatically after a restart" set to off. Windows no longer stores your sign-in to auto-sign-in and lock after an update restart. Sophia sets the per-user ARSO OptOut under a SID-keyed key instead, which the engine cannot address; the policy is machine-wide.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Security-minded users, shared PCs
tweaks.tradeoff: After an update restart you sign in yourself, and apps registered for restart do not reopen until you do.
tweaks.managedSkip: Sign-in behaviour is set by the organisation's policies (Intune or Group Policy).

tweaks.description: Disable the Windows PowerShell 2.0 engine (optional feature).
tweaks.revert: Snapshot per step: -Undo runs Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature if the feature was enabled (the payload stays on disk, so no download).
tweaks.explanation: Hardening: PowerShell 2.0 has none of the logging and AMSI protections of 5.1, so attackers use 'powershell -version 2' to slip past them. Disabling the feature removes that downgrade path. Microsoft removed the feature from Windows 11 24H2 builds in 2025, so on current builds the engine will skip it as not present; it matters on older or unpatched installs.
tweaks.whoBenefits: Any PC that still has the feature
tweaks.tradeoff: Very old scripts or installers that require PowerShell 2.0 stop working. The feature payload stays on disk, so undo works offline.
